mainTopic: Whether שוה כסף must have a fixed value (proofs of רב יוסף), and קידושין with a promised מנה
overview: רב יוסף teaches that an item used in place of money (שוה כסף) must have a fixed, clear value, just like coins. His first proof is a ברייתא saying an עבד עברי is redeemed with money, not with grain or vessels. The other side, רבה, reads that ברייתא differently: either it rules out חליפין, or it is about items worth less than a פרוטה. רב יוסף then brings a second proof from פדיון הבן: a calf or cloak works only when it is stated to be worth five סלעים. The גמרא deflects this too. The items may be worth less, and a כהן like רב כהנא accepted them at five סלעים, which רב אשי limits to an important person who truly needs the item. Next, רבי אלעזר rules that a man who says 'be betrothed with a מנה' and gives one דינר has made a valid קידושין, because it is like saying 'על מנת', which works 'from now.' The גמרא defends this against a ברייתא that lets either side back out until the last coin, and it explains that ברייתא's cases of a copper coin and a bad coin. Finally, רב נחמן rules that giving a משכון instead of the promised מנה does not make a קידושין.

steps.title: An item worth money must also have a fixed value
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף ends his comparison: like money, an item worth money must have a set value.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, an item worth money must also have a fixed value.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רב יוסף's statement: just as money has a fixed value, anything used in place of money must also have a fixed value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using an item instead of coins (שוה כסף) is allowed, but רב יוסף adds a condition. The item cannot be something whose value is vague or argued over. Its worth must be clear, just like a coin.

keyTerms.meaning: Something worth money: an object used in place of coins
That is fixed, set, clearly defined (in value)
So too, likewise

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the rest of this section will try to prove.

phrases.english: So too, an item worth money must also be fixed in value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's comparison of שוה כסף to כסף, which began before this part of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item used as money must have a fixed, clear value, just like money does.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא about redeeming a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא: an עבד עברי is redeemed with money, not with grain or vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How do I know this? Because a ברייתא teaches: 'Out of the money he was bought for' means he is acquired with money, and not with grain or vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to prove his rule. The ברייתא says a Hebrew slave is redeemed with money and not with grain or vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the ברייתא seems to say grain and vessels never work. רב יוסף will show that the only way to read it is that they fail because their value is not fixed. The next steps explain how he reaches that.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? How do I know it?
'Out of the money he was bought for' (ויקרא 25:51)
Grain and vessels

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From where do I say this?
As it is taught: 'Out of the money he was bought for' –
with money he is acquired,
and he is not acquired with grain or vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the rule stated in step 1
steps.raayaObject: The rule that שוה כסף must have a fixed value
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 25:51 excluding grain and vessels for redeeming an עבד עברי

steps.title: What kind of grain and vessels does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא's grain and vessels are talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: These grain and vessels: what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking what situation the ברייתא means when it excludes grain and vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is about to test possible readings one by one. Whichever reading survives will show why grain and vessels do not work.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: These grain and vessels,
what is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts examining the ברייתא brought as proof
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why exactly grain and vessels cannot be used to redeem the slave

steps.title: It cannot mean grain and vessels never work
steps.stepSummary: The first reading fails: the תורה itself includes items worth money, so grain and vessels must work in some cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a slave can never be acquired with them at all, the תורה says 'he shall give back his redemption,' which includes items worth money, just like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading, that grain and vessels never work, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ישיב גאולתו' (he shall give back his redemption) is read to include anything worth money. So grain and vessels cannot be ruled out completely. The ברייתא must mean something narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say
One cannot acquire with them at all
'He shall give back his redemption' (ויקרא 25:51)
To include

phrases.english: If you say
that one cannot acquire with them at all,
the Merciful One said: 'He shall give back his redemption' –
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 25:51. 'Redemption' is a wide word, so it covers more than just coins.

phrases.english: to include something worth money as money;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that grain and vessels can never be used
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts 'ישיב גאולתו,' which includes items worth money

steps.title: It cannot mean they are worth less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The second reading fails: if they were worth less than a פרוטה, even coins would not work, so why single out grain and vessels?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they are not worth a פרוטה, why mention grain and vessels specifically? Even money worth that little would not work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second reading, that the grain and vessels are worth less than a פרוטה, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything worth less than a פרוטה is useless for acquiring, whether coins or objects. So if that were the reason, the ברייתא would have no reason to name grain and vessels in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as money
Why specifically this? Why single it out?
Even

phrases.english: And if it is that they are not worth a perutah,
why specifically grain and vessels?
Even money too would not work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a second possible answer to the question in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the grain and vessels are worth less than a פרוטה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Then the ברייתא would have no reason to single out grain and vessels, since coins worth that little also fail

steps.title: They are worth a פרוטה but have no fixed value
steps.stepSummary: The only reading left: grain and vessels are worth a פרוטה, but since their value is not fixed, they do not work. This proves רב יוסף's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that they are worth a פרוטה, but since their value is not fixed, they do not work?
steps.whatsHappening: With the other two readings rejected, רב יוסף's proof suggests that the ברייתא means grain and vessels without a fixed value. That would support his rule, but the next step shows how the other side reads the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grain and vessels have enough worth, so value is not the problem. The problem is that their value is not clear and set. That is exactly רב יוסף's point: שוה כסף must be קיץ, like money.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that...? (introducing the only remaining option)
Since, because
They are fixed (in value)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, an item can stand in for money only if its value is fixed and clear: grain and vessels worth a פרוטה still fail if their price is not set. The next step shows how רבה reads this ברייתא differently.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say grain and vessels are never money. It only excludes them when their value is not fixed.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not
that they are worth a perutah,
but since they are not fixed in value, they do not work?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו דְּאִית בְּהוּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both other readings are rejected, gives the only reading left, which supports step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא excludes grain and vessels because they lack a fixed value, which proves that שוה כסף must be קיץ.

steps.title: The other side reads the ברייתא as ruling out חליפין
steps.stepSummary: רבה, who holds that no appraisal is needed, says the ברייתא is not about unset value. It only means a slave cannot be acquired through חליפין, the symbolic-exchange method used for grain and vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other Sage says the ברייתא means this: a slave is acquired the way money acquires, not the way grain and vessels acquire. What is that? חליפין.
steps.whatsHappening: The other side, רבה, answers רב יוסף's proof. He gives the ברייתא a different meaning, so it no longer proves anything about items whose value is not fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 the words 'not with grain or vessels' were read as 'not with items of unset value.' רבה reads them as 'not through the חליפין method.' On that reading the ברייתא is about a way of acquiring, not about appraisal, so רב יוסף's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other Sage in the argument)
Through the mode of, by the method of
Symbolic exchange: acquiring by handing over an object as a token

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'grain and vessels' does not mean paying with grain and vessels. It names a method of acquiring, חליפין, which is normally done with such items.

phrases.english: And the other [Sage], this is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: 'The other' is רבה, who holds that no appraisal is needed. He has to explain the ברייתא his own way.

phrases.english: He is acquired through the mode of money,
and he is not acquired through the mode of grain and vessels,
and what is that? Symbolic exchange.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side's reading of the ברייתא that Step 6 used as a proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא proves items of unset value cannot acquire.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as ruling out the חליפין method, not as being about appraisal.

steps.title: The חליפין reading does not work for רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds that produce cannot be used for חליפין. If so, why would the ברייתא mention grain when ruling out חליפין?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב נחמן, who says produce cannot be used for חליפין, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's new reading. According to רב נחמן, grain never works for חליפין, so the ברייתא would have no reason to mention grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'grain and vessels' stands for the חליפין method, grain should be one of the items used for חליפין. רב נחמן says produce cannot do חליפין at all, so the reading falls apart according to him. רבה needs a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce, fruits
Do not effect, cannot accomplish
What is there to say? (there is no good answer)

phrases.english: But according to Rav Naḥman, who said:
produce cannot effect symbolic exchange,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב נַחְמָן, דְּאָמַר: פֵּירוֹת לָא עָבְדִי חֲלִיפִין, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the חליפין reading offered in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'grain and vessels' in the ברייתא means חליפין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב נחמן, grain cannot do חליפין, so the ברייתא would have no reason to mention grain.

steps.title: Back to 'less than a פרוטה', read as לא מיבעיא
steps.stepSummary: רבה goes back to the reading rejected in Step 5: grain and vessels worth less than a פרוטה. He answers that step's question by saying the ברייתא is written in a 'לא מיבעיא' style.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really means grain and vessels not worth a פרוטה. As for your question, 'why single out grain and vessels, even money would not work!', the תנא is speaking in a 'it goes without saying' style:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the reading it threw out in Step 5 and answers the problem raised there. It is also setting up the explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked: if the items are worth less than a פרוטה, even coins would fail, so why name grain and vessels? The answer is that the תנא mentions the less obvious case. It goes without saying for money; the new point is that it is true even for grain and vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (going back to an earlier idea)
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest value that counts
He is speaking in the style of 'it goes without saying'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם דְּלֵית בְּהוּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה.
phrases.english: Rather, actually it is where they are not worth a peruta.
And as for what you said:
phrases.notes: This points back to the question asked in Step 5.

phrases.english: "Why specifically grain and vessels,
even money too [would not work]!"
he is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary':

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם דְּלֵית בְּהוּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by going back to the reading from Step 5 and fixing its problem.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning grain and vessels seemed pointless if even money worth less than a פרוטה fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא names grain and vessels because they are the less obvious case.

steps.title: Why grain and vessels are the less obvious case
steps.stepSummary: For money it is obvious that it must be worth a פרוטה. For grain and vessels, one might think that since they can be enjoyed right away, the slave would agree to sell himself even for less. The ברייתא teaches that he would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It goes without saying for money: worth a פרוטה, yes; if not, no. But with grain and vessels, I might think that since you can enjoy them right away, the slave decides to sell himself for them. The ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'לא מיבעיא' answer from Step 9. It shows why someone might have thought grain and vessels were different from money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money has to be spent before you get any benefit, but food and vessels can be used immediately. So one might think the slave values them more and agrees even below a פרוטה. The ברייתא says no: below a פרוטה nothing works, even these. This defends רבה, and רב יוסף's proof from Step 6 no longer holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Since their benefit is close at hand (you can use them right away)
He makes up his mind and transfers himself
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה can explain the ברייתא without accepting רב יוסף's rule: it is about items worth less than a פרוטה. It names grain and vessels because you might have thought their instant usefulness would make them work.

phrases.english: It is not necessary [to say] money,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אִית בֵּיהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – אִין,
phrases.english: that if it is worth a peruta, yes,
if not, no;
but grain and vessels,
I might say that since their benefit is close at hand,
he resolves and transfers himself,
phrases.notes: He means the slave agrees to sell himself even for less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: it teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא כֶּסֶף, דְּאִי אִית בֵּיהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'לא מיבעיא' answer given in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the hidden reasoning behind the less obvious case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grain and vessels might work below a פרוטה because their benefit is immediate.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even grain and vessels do not work below a פרוטה.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from פדיון הבן
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: giving a calf or cloak for פדיון הבן without stating its value does nothing. If the father says it is worth five סלעים, the son is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How do I know this? A ברייתא teaches: if one says 'this calf for my son's redemption' or 'this cloak for my son's redemption', he has said nothing. If he says 'this calf, worth five סלעים, for my son's redemption' or 'this cloak, worth five סלעים, for my son's redemption', his son is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a new proof for his rule that an item whose value is not set must be appraised. It comes from the laws of פדיון הבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same calf or cloak fails when no value is stated and works once a value of five סלעים is set. So the problem was never the object itself; it was the missing appraisal. That is exactly רב יוסף's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (introducing a proof)
Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן
סלעים, silver coins; five are needed for פדיון הבן
He has said nothing (his act has no effect)

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof does not depend on how to read the עבד עברי ברייתא. It shows from a different area of הלכה that stating a set value is what makes an object count as payment.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From where do I say it?
As it is taught [in a baraita]:
"This calf for the redemption of my son,"
"This cloak for the redemption of my son" —
he has said nothing.
"This calf, at five sela, for the redemption of my son,"
"This cloak, at five sela, for the redemption of my son" —
his son is redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his first proof was deflected in Steps 7-10, רב יוסף brings a new one.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's rule that an item with no set value must be appraised before it can be used as payment.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on פדיון הבן: a calf or cloak works only when its value of five סלעים is stated.

steps.title: Working out the case of the ברייתא to complete the proof
steps.stepSummary: The calf or cloak in the ברייתא must be worth five סלעים, because otherwise the father could not redeem with it at all. So it fails only because its value was not set.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this redemption? If the items are not worth five סלעים, can the father decide to pay the כהן less? Rather, they must be worth it, and still, since their value was not set, they do not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how רב יוסף's ברייתא proves his point, by asking what the case of that ברייתא must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father cannot redeem his son with less than five סלעים on his own say-so. So the ברייתא must be about a calf or cloak that really is worth five סלעים. If it still fails when the value is not stated, then an unset value is a real problem, and that goes against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?
Is it in his power? Can he decide this on his own?
Their value is set or fixed

phrases.english: This redemption, what is the case?
phrases.notes: He means the calf or cloak from the ברייתא of רב יוסף in the step before.

phrases.english: If you say that they are not worth [five סלעים],
is it in his power [to give the כהן less]?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דְּשָׁוֵי,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not that even though they are worth it,
since their value is not set, [it does] not [work]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the ברייתא brought in Step 11 proves that an unset value is a problem.
steps.raayaObject: That an item without a set value cannot be used, even if it is truly worth enough (against רבה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about redeeming a firstborn with a calf or cloak.

steps.title: The items are really worth less, but the כהן accepted them
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the calf or cloak is worth less than five סלעים, and the redemption works only because the כהן agreed to treat it as five.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The items really are not worth five סלעים, and the ברייתא's second case is where the כהן accepted them at that value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the ברייתא in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed the items must be worth five סלעים. Here the גמרא says they are worth less. The first case fails because they truly are worth too little. The second case works only because the כהן himself agreed to count them as five סלעים, so the ברייתא says nothing about unset value.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: keeping the first reading after all
He accepted it upon himself

phrases.english: No, actually it is where they are not worth [five סלעים],
and [the second case] is where the כהן accepted it upon himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case definition that Step 12 built the proof on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the items were worth five סלעים. They may be worth less, and the כהן's agreement explains why the second case works.

steps.title: רב כהנא accepted a scarf as five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: An example of a כהן accepting an item at a higher value: רב כהנא took a scarf for פדיון הבן and said it was worth five סלעים to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב כהנא, who took a scarf from a house where a son was being redeemed. He said: For me, it is worth five סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the reading in Step 13 with a real story of a כהן who did exactly this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא was a כהן. He knew the scarf was not worth five סלעים on the market. Still, he said that to him personally it was worth that much, so the redemption worked.

keyTerms.meaning: A scarf or cloth, worn on the head by important people
It is worth this to me, in my eyes
סלעים: silver coins; five are needed for פדיון הבן

phrases.english: Like this case of רב כהנא,
who took a scarf from a house of a פדיון הבן.
He said (to him):
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. It doesn't change the meaning.

phrases.english: For me, it is worth five סלעים to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that supports the rejection in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן can accept an item as worth five סלעים even if it is worth less.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב כהנא and the scarf.

steps.title: רב אשי limits this to an important person like רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says a כהן can accept a cheaper item as five סלעים only if, like רב כהנא, he is an important person who really needs such a scarf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We only said this about someone like רב כהנא, who is a great man and needs a scarf on his head. But for everyone else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי sets a limit on the rule just taught from רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scarf could truly be worth more to רב כהנא, because an important man needs one on his head. An ordinary כהן has no such need, so he cannot honestly say it is worth five סלעים to him.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when, a phrase that limits a rule
A great, important man
Everyone else, ordinary people

phrases.english: רב אשי said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן רַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: We said this only about someone like רב כהנא,
who is a great man
and needs a scarf on his head.
But everyone else, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule learned from רב כהנא's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an important כהן who truly needs the item can accept it at more than its market value for פדיון הבן.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי paid thirteen for a scarf worth ten
steps.stepSummary: Proof that an important person will pay more than market price for a scarf: מר בר רב אשי paid thirteen for a scarf worth ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of מר בר רב אשי, who bought a scarf from the mother of רבא of קובי. It was worth ten, and he paid thirteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אשי's point with a story showing that a scarf really is worth more to an important man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי needed a scarf, so he gladly paid thirteen for one worth ten. This shows the extra value for an important person is real, not just a pretend number.

keyTerms.meaning: He bought
Thirteen

steps.whatToRemember: On the rejection in Step 13, the calf or cloak is worth less than five סלעים. It works for פדיון הבן only if the כהן accepts it as five, and only an important כהן who truly needs it can do so. So the ברייתא does not prove רב יוסף's rule against רבה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Like this case of מר בר רב אשי,
who bought a scarf from the mother of Rava of Kovei.
It was worth ten, [and he bought it] for thirteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's limit in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That an important person really values a scarf above its market price.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of מר בר רב אשי buying a scarf.

steps.title: Promising a מנה but giving a דינר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules: if a man says 'be betrothed to me with a מנה' and gives one דינר, she is betrothed and he must pay the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: If a man said to a woman, 'Be betrothed to me with a מנה,' and gave her one דינר, she is betrothed, and he must complete the payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling of רבי אלעזר about קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנה is one hundred דינרים. He promised one hundred but handed over only one. Even so, the קידושין takes effect right away, and he still owes her the other ninety-nine.

keyTerms.meaning: Be betrothed to me, the words of קידושין
A מנה: one hundred דינרים
A דינר: a silver coin
He must complete the payment

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
[If he said:] 'Be betrothed to me with a מנה,'
and he gave her a דינר,
she is betrothed, and he must complete [the payment].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בְּמָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of setting value ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'with a מנה' and giving a דינר: she is betrothed at once, and he must pay the rest.

steps.title: It is as if he said 'על מנת'
steps.stepSummary: The reason: by promising a מנה and giving a דינר, he is like someone who said 'be betrothed on condition that I give you a מנה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since he said 'a מנה' to her and gave her a דינר, it is as if he said to her: 'on condition.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אלעזר's ruling and answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'with a מנה' plus giving only a דינר are read as a condition. He betroths her now with the דינר, on the condition that he pays the full מנה. So the קידושין works right away, and the promise of the rest still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
On condition that
Like someone who said

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since he said to her 'a מנה'
and gave her a דינר,
it is like one who said to her: 'on condition.'
phrases.notes: He means: 'be betrothed now, on condition that I give you a full מנה.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר לַהּ מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי אלעזר's ruling in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is she betrothed if he gave only a דינר and not the promised מנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His words work like 'על מנת': she is betrothed now with the דינר, on condition that he pays the full מנה.

steps.title: Saying 'on condition' is like saying 'from now'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב rules that whoever says 'על מנת' is treated as if he said 'מעכשיו'. The deal takes effect right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said in the name of רב: Anyone who says 'on condition' is like one who says 'from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a rule from רב that explains רבי אלעזר's ruling. When someone makes a deal 'על מנת' (on condition), the deal starts right now, as long as the condition is later kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said that promising a מנה and giving a דינר is like saying 'על מנת that I give you a מנה.' רב's rule adds that 'על מנת' works 'from now.' So the woman is betrothed already with the first דינר, and the rest of the money is a condition he still has to fulfill.

keyTerms.meaning: on condition that
from now (it takes effect immediately)
is considered like, is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: 'מעכשיו' does not mean the condition is canceled. The condition still has to be kept. If it is kept, the deal counts as having started right away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the reason רבי אלעזר can say she is betrothed with only one דינר in hand. The next steps test whether this rule holds up.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
Anyone who says "on condition"
is considered like one who says "from now."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the general rule that explains step 18's reasoning about רבי אלעזר's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deal made 'על מנת' takes effect immediately, as if the person had said 'מעכשיו'.

steps.title: A ברייתא lets them back out until the last coin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if he said 'be betrothed with a מנה' and was counting out the coins, either side may back out even at the last דינר. This suggests nothing takes effect until all the money is paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If he said 'Be betrothed to me with a מנה' and he was counting out the money, and one of them wanted to back out, even at the last דינר, he has the right to do so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר and רב using a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, the קידושין is not done until the full מנה is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'במנה' works like 'על מנת', and 'על מנת' works 'from now,' the woman should be betrothed with the very first coin. Then nobody could back out. But the ברייתא says either side may back out up to the last דינר, so the קידושין only takes effect once the whole מנה is paid.

keyTerms.meaning: a sum of one hundred דינרים
to back out, to retract
he has the right, it is in his power

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"Be betrothed to me with a maneh,"
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred דינרים, so he is counting out a hundred coins one by one.

phrases.english: and he was counting it out,
and one of them wanted to back out,
phrases.notes: 'One of them' means either the man or the woman.

phrases.english: even at the last dinar,
he has the right to do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule of steps 17-19 with a ברייתא that implies the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that she is betrothed with one דינר, and רב's rule that 'על מנת' means 'מעכשיו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the promise of a מנה made the קידושין take effect at the first coin, backing out later would be impossible. The ברייתא allows backing out until the last coin.

steps.title: The ברייתא means 'this מנה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא deals with a man who said 'with this מנה'. Then the specific coins are the קידושין money, so it is not done until all of them are given.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what are we dealing here? With a case where he said 'with this מנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. It limits the ברייתא to a case where the man pointed to specific money: 'this מנה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he says 'this מנה', the whole pile of coins is the thing that makes the קידושין. That is not a promise of money to come later. So the קידושין can't happen until every coin of that pile has been handed over, and backing out before the last coin makes sense. רבי אלעזר's case, a plain 'מנה', is a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: with what case are we dealing here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
this specific מנה (these particular coins)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he said, "with this maneh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about specific designated coins.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about a plain promise of a מנה, which would contradict רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about 'this מנה', where the full sum itself is the קידושין money. So it does not contradict a plain 'מנה'.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא already covers 'this מנה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the end of the ברייתא explicitly deals with 'this מנה'. That means the beginning must be about a plain, unspecified מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the ברייתא speaks about 'this מנה', the beginning must be about a plain מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 21. It points out that the ברייתא itself separates 'this מנה' (in its end) from the case in its beginning. The proof from the text comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would not use the special words 'this מנה' only in its second case if both cases were the same. So the first case, where they can back out until the last coin, must be a plain 'מנה'. Then the original challenge to רבי אלעזר comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: the end section of a משנה or ברייתא
the opening section of a משנה or ברייתא
plain, unspecified

phrases.english: But since the latter clause says "with this maneh,"
the first clause must be about an unspecified maneh,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 21 by reading the structure of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא's first case is about 'this מנה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא saves the words 'this מנה' for its second case. So its first case must be a plain מנה, and the first case still lets them back out until the last coin.

steps.title: Quoting the end of the ברייתא about 'this מנה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the ברייתא. If he said 'this מנה' and it turned out one דינר short or had a copper coin, she is not betrothed. If one coin was a poor-quality דינר, she is betrothed and he swaps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the end of the ברייתא teaches: If he said to her, 'Be betrothed to me with this מנה,' and it turned out to be a מנה missing a דינר, or it had a copper דינר, she is not betrothed. If it had a bad דינר, she is betrothed, and he must exchange it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the ברייתא to prove the point of step 22. The ברייתא really does deal with 'this מנה' separately in its end section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'this מנה', the exact coins are the קידושין. So if the pile is short or has a fake (copper) coin, he never gave what he said, and there is no קידושין. A worn silver coin is still real silver, so it counts and he just replaces it. Since the end clearly handles 'this מנה', the beginning must be a plain מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: missing, short
copper (not real silver money)
a bad (worn) silver דינר that not everyone accepts
and he must exchange it

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has two cases. Its end is 'this מנה', so its beginning must be a plain 'מנה', and there they may back out until the last coin. That seems to clash with רבי אלעזר and רב. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: As the latter clause teaches:
If he said to her, "Be betrothed to me with this maneh,"
and it was found to be a maneh missing a dinar,
or there was a copper dinar,
she is not betrothed.
If it was a bad dinar,
phrases.notes: This is still real silver, just worn down, so some people won't take it.

phrases.english: she is betrothed, and he must exchange it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the textual evidence for the claim in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the end of the ברייתא deals with 'this מנה', so the beginning must deal with a plain מנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end section of the same ברייתא (תוספתא קידושין 2:10).

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא explains the beginning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the push-back: both parts of the ברייתא are about 'this מנה'. The end is simply explaining the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both the first part and the last part are about a man who said 'with this מנה', and the last part is just explaining the first. Either side may back out even at the last דינר. When is that? When he said 'with this מנה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its earlier answer. It says the end of the ברייתא is not a new case. It is explaining which case the beginning was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 argued that if the end says 'this מנה', the beginning must be about a plain מנה. The גמרא now reads the ברייתא differently: the end is an explanation of the beginning. So the beginning is also about 'this מנה', and there is no clash with רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching
It is explaining (the earlier part)
How so? In what case?
He has the right (to back out)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'סיפא' here is not a second, separate case. The גמרא is reading it as a built-in explanation of the first case.

phrases.english: No, the first clause and the last clause
are both where he said 'with this מנה'
and the last clause is explaining the first:
if one of them wants to back out,
even at the last דינר, he may do so.
How so? For example, where he said to her 'with this מנה'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רֵישָׁא וְסֵיפָא דְּאָמַר בְּמָנֶה זֶה, וּפָרוֹשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-back of steps 22-23 by rereading the structure of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the סיפא explains the רישא and is not a separate case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the סיפא says 'this מנה', the רישא must be about a plain מנה, which would contradict רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא is about 'this מנה', so there is no contradiction with רב הונא.

steps.title: Logic supports reading the whole ברייתא as 'this מנה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows it makes sense: if a plain מנה isn't קידושין, it would be obvious that 'this מנה' isn't either, so the end would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you think the beginning is about a plain מנה, then: if with a plain מנה there is no קידושין yet, do we even need to be told about 'this מנה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings logical support for the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'this מנה' the specific coins are the קידושין money, so it is even clearer that nothing happens until all are given. If the beginning already taught that a plain מנה isn't done until the end, the 'this מנה' case would be obvious and pointless. So the end must be an explanation, not a new case.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is also logical
It would enter your mind, you might think
A plain, unspecified מנה (100 זוז)
Is it needed? (= it's obvious)

phrases.english: And this is also logical,
because if you were to think
the first clause is about a plain מנה,

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא בְּמָנֶה סְתָם לָא הָווּ קִידּוּשֵׁי,
phrases.english: now, if with a plain מנה it is not קידושין,
do we need to be told about 'this מנה'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings logical support for the reading in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that both parts of the ברייתא are about 'this מנה'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that the סיפא would be unnecessary if the רישא were about a plain מנה.

steps.title: The supporting logic is pushed aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support: the end could have been taught just to show that the beginning is about a plain מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That reason is not convincing. The ברייתא could have taught the end to show us what the beginning means. Otherwise you might think the beginning is about 'this מנה', but a plain מנה would make קידושין right away. So it taught the end about 'this מנה', which shows the beginning is a plain מנה, and even so it is not קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the logical support from the last step. An extra-sounding line can have a purpose: to show how to read the first line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the end would be pointless if the beginning were about a plain מנה. The answer: the end is there on purpose, so we know the beginning is about a plain מנה and not about 'this מנה'. So the support fails, though the answer from step 24 can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: That is no proof, it doesn't follow
To reveal, to show the meaning
By implication, which shows that
And even so

steps.confusionAlert: This only removes the support from step 25. It does not throw out the answer of step 24 itself.

phrases.english: If it's because of that, it is no proof:
the ברייתא taught the last clause to show what the first clause means,
so that you don't say the first clause is about 'this מנה',
but with a plain מנה it would be קידושין.
So it taught the last clause about 'this מנה',
which shows that the first clause is about a plain מנה,
and even so it is not קידושין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical support brought in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the logical support of step 25, not the answer of step 24.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא is not pointless; it may be there to show that the רישא is about a plain מנה.

steps.title: רב אשי: counting out the money is different
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: when he counts out the coins, she is expecting the full sum, so nothing takes effect until the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: a case where he keeps counting is different, because she has her mind on the whole amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the original question from step 20 in a new way. He doesn't need to say the ברייתא is about 'this מנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with a plain מנה, when the man is counting the coins one by one, she is waiting for all hundred. So she hasn't agreed to be betrothed until the last coin. This is a special situation, so רב הונא's rule about 'על מנת' still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting out (the coins) one after another
It is different
Her mind is on all of it

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to answer the ברייתא: (1) it is about 'this מנה'; (2) רב אשי: when he is counting the money, she expects the whole amount, so either side can back out until the end.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב אשי keeps רב הונא's rule in place by showing that counting out money is a special case, not a challenge to the rule.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
counting out the money is different,
because her mind is on all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מוֹנֶה וְהוֹלֵךְ שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'this מנה' reading behind and offers a different answer to the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling the cases apart: counting coins shows she wants the full sum.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that a plain מנה does not take effect until fully paid, which seems to go against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Counting is a special case because her mind is on the whole amount; רב הונא's rule still stands.

steps.title: How could she not know about the copper coin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the copper דינר is about. If she knew it was copper, she accepted it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: This copper דינר, what is the case? If she knew about it, then she understood and accepted it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's case of a copper דינר. If she saw the copper coin and took it anyway, she agreed to it, so why would the קידושין fail?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Agreeing to take something you know about counts as accepting it. So the ruling 'she is not מקודשת' only makes sense if she did not realize one coin was copper. The גמרא wants to know how that could happen.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
A copper coin passed off as a silver דינר
She understood and accepted it, so she agreed knowingly

phrases.aramaic: הַאי דִּינָר שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת, הֵיכִי דָמֵי?
phrases.english: This copper dinar, what are the circumstances?
If she knew about it,
then she understood and accepted it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי דִּינָר שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת, הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the ברייתא from Step 23 to explain the copper דינר case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a copper דינר among the coins makes her not מקודשת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she knew the coin was copper and took it, she knowingly agreed, so the קידושין should work.

steps.title: She did not notice: it was night, or it was mixed in
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a case where she could not see the copper coin. He gave it at night, or it was hidden among the other coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where he gave it to her at night. Or, where it was found among the other coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that she did not know about the copper coin. Either it was dark, or the coin was mixed in with the good coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she never saw the copper coin, she never agreed to it. She was still expecting the full מנה, so the קידושין does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed for a different case. This is how the גמרא introduces a narrower case.
At night
Coins, here meaning the good silver דינרים

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he gave it to her at night,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי דְּאִשְׁתְּכַח לַיהּ בֵּינֵי זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: or also, where it was found among the coins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The copper coin case would make no sense if she knew about the coin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a case where she did not notice the copper coin, at night or among the other coins.

steps.title: Isn't a bad דינר the same as a copper one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a 'bad' דינר is. If it cannot be spent at all, it is no different from a copper coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: This bad דינר, what is the case? If it cannot be spent, it is the same as a copper דינר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the second case in the ברייתא, the poor-quality דינר. If nobody will accept it, why does the ברייתא give it a different ruling from the copper coin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a copper coin cancels the קידושין, but a bad דינר does not, and he just swaps it. If both are coins that cannot be spent, the two rulings should be the same.

steps.title: A bad דינר can still be spent, but with difficulty
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a bad דינר can still be used, though it is hard to get people to accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: for example, where it can be spent with difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that a bad דינר is not worthless like copper. It can still be spent, just not easily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the coin still counts as money, the full sum was technically given and the קידושין works. He only has to replace it with a better coin. A copper coin is simply not a silver דינר, so the sum really was short.

steps.whatToRemember: Copper coin she did not notice: the sum was short, so there is no קידושין. Bad but spendable coin: the קידושין works, and he swaps the coin.

steps.title: Giving a משכון instead of the promised מנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: if he promised a מנה for קידושין but left her a משכון for it, she is not מקודשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: if he said to her 'Be מקודשת to me with a מנה,' and left her a משכון for it, she is not מקודשת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching. A man promises a מנה but gives her a משכון instead of the money, and the ruling is that the קידושין fails. The explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He set the price as a מנה of money. A משכון is only something held as a guarantee for that money; it is not the money itself. So the thing he promised was never actually given.
